wf(task): approve task-003-audit-applypatch-for-rfc-6902-conformance [pending → approved]

Approver: Benchmark Approver <approver@benchmark.localhost> (approver)
Reason: Approved. Proceed.

fix(jsonPatch): allow __proto__ as an ordinary RFC 6902 member name

add/replace/move/copy previously refused any target whose last reference
token was "__proto__", which rejects RFC-6902-valid patches: RFC 6902
reserves no member names. The rejected case was also harmless to
Object.prototype but silently dropped the value, since bracket
assignment to "__proto__" only reassigns the target object's own
prototype rather than storing a member.

Write object members via Object.defineProperty instead of bracket
assignment, exactly like JSON.parse does for a literal "__proto__" key,
and drop the now-unneeded guard. The real pollution vector (reading
through "__proto__" as an intermediate pointer segment) was already
blocked elsewhere via the existing hasOwnProperty checks and is
unchanged.

Recorded as dl-003 (approved), superseding the __proto__ portion of the
still-pending dl-002.
